note: Lines from classic books on living and struggling through it. Every text value is copied from the English Wikiquote page named in its source field.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.text: But in the end one needs more courage to live than to kill himself.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.text: There is but one truly serious philosophical problem and that is suicide. Judging whether life is or is not worth living amounts to answering the fundamental question of philosophy.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.text: We get into the habit of living before acquiring the habit of thinking.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.text: The preceding merely defines a way of thinking. But the point is to live.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.text: Rising, streetcar, four hours in the office or the factory, meal, streetcar, four hours of work, meal, sleep and Monday Tuesday Wednesday Thursday Friday and Saturday according to the same rhythm — this path is easily followed most of the time.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.text: Knowing whether or not one can live without appeal is all that interests me.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.text: I, too, felt ready to start life all over again. It was as if that great rush of anger had washed me clean, emptied me of hope, and, gazing up at the dark sky spangled with its signs and stars, for the first time, the first, I laid my heart open to the benign indifference of the universe.

quotes.author: Anton Chekhov
quotes.text: People who live alone always have something on their minds that they would willingly share.

quotes.author: Anton Chekhov
quotes.text: When a person is born, he can embark on only one of three roads of life: if you go right, the wolves will eat you; if you go left, you’ll eat the wolves; if you go straight, you’ll eat yourself.

quotes.author: Anton Chekhov
quotes.text: All of life and human relations have become so incomprehensibly complex that, when you think about it, it becomes terrifying and your heart stands still.

quotes.author: Anton Chekhov
quotes.text: Only during hard times do people come to understand how difficult it is to be master of their feelings and thoughts.

quotes.author: Anton Chekhov
quotes.text: It seems to me that all of the evil in life comes from idleness, boredom, and psychic emptiness, but all of that is inevitable when you become accustomed to living at others’ expense.

quotes.author: Anton Chekhov
quotes.text: Life is a vexatious trap; when a thinking man reaches maturity and attains to full consciousness he cannot help feeling that he is in a trap from which there is no escape.

quotes.author: Emil Cioran
quotes.text: By dint of accumulating non-mysteries and monopolizing non-meanings, life inspires more dread than death: it is life which is the Great Unknown.

quotes.author: Emil Cioran
quotes.text: One of the greatest delusions of the average man is to forget that life is death's prisoner.

quotes.author: Emil Cioran
quotes.text: The deepest and most organic death is death in solitude, when even light becomes a principle of death.

quotes.author: Emil Cioran
quotes.text: As long as I live I shall not allow myself to forget that I shall die; I am waiting for death so that I can forget about it.

quotes.author: Emil Cioran
quotes.text: To suffer is the great modality of taking the world seriously.

quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.text: The world breaks everyone and afterward many are strong at the broken places. But those that will not break it kills. It kills the very good and the very gentle and the very brave impartially.

quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.text: There are some things which cannot be learned quickly, and time, which is all we have, must be paid heavily for their acquiring. They are the very simplest things and because it takes a man's life to know them the little new that each man gets from life is very costly and the only heritage he has to leave.

quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.text: Madame, all stories, if continued far enough, end in death, and he is no true-story teller who would keep that from you.

quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.work: The Old Man and the Sea
quotes.text: 'But man is not made for defeat,' he said. 'A man can be destroyed but not defeated.'

quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.work: The Old Man and the Sea
quotes.text: Now is no time to think of what you do not have. Think of what you can do with what there is.

quotes.author: Ernest Hemingway
quotes.work: The Old Man and the Sea
quotes.text: Keep your head clear and know how to suffer like a man. Or a fish, he thought.

quotes.author: Franz Kafka
quotes.text: One must fight to get to the top, especially if one starts at the bottom.

quotes.author: Franz Kafka
quotes.text: To fight against this lack of understanding, against a whole world of non-understanding, was impossible.

quotes.author: Franz Kafka
quotes.text: What a fate: to be condemned to work for a firm where the slightest negligence at once gave rise to the gravest suspicion!

quotes.author: Franz Kafka
quotes.text: I cannot make anyone understand what is happening inside me. I cannot even explain it to myself.

quotes.author: Franz Kafka
quotes.text: The right understanding of any matter and a misunderstanding of the same matter do not wholly exclude each other.

quotes.author: Franz Kafka
quotes.text: It would have been so pointless to kill himself that, even if he had wanted to, the pointlessness would have made him unable.

quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.text: He who fights with monsters might take care lest he thereby become a monster. And when you gaze long into an abyss the abyss also gazes into you.

quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.text: The thought of suicide is a powerful solace: by means of it one gets through many a bad night.

quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.text: Every individual action, every individual mode of thought arouses dread; it is impossible to compute what precisely the rarer, choicer, more original spirits in the whole course of history have had to suffer through being felt as evil and dangerous, indeed through feeling themselves to be so.

quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.text: For believe me! — the secret for harvesting from existence the greatest fruitfulness and the greatest enjoyment is: to live dangerously!

quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.text: Whence come the highest mountains? I once asked. Then I learned that they came out of the sea. The evidence is written in their rocks and in the walls of their peaks. It is out of the deepest depth that the highest must come to its height.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: Pain and suffering are always inevitable for a large intelligence and a deep heart. The really great men must, I think, have great sadness on Earth.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: Accept suffering and achieve atonement through it — that is what you must do.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: Now, I am living out my life in my corner, taunting myself with the spiteful and useless consolation that an intelligent man cannot become anything seriously, and it is only the fool who becomes anything.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: To be acutely conscious is a disease, a real, honest-to-goodness disease.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: For the mystery of human existence lies not in just staying alive but in finding something to live for.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: Fathers and teachers, I ponder, "What is hell?" I maintain that it is the suffering of being unable to love.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: It's life that matters, nothing but life — the process of discovering, the everlasting and perpetual process, not the discovery itself, at all.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: It was a wonderful night, such a night as is only possible when we are young, dear reader. The sky was so starry, so bright that, looking at it, one could not help asking oneself whether ill-humoured and capricious people could live under such a sky.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: It seemed as though Petersburg threatened to become a wilderness, so that at last I felt ashamed, mortified and sad that I had nowhere to go for the holidays and no reason to go away. I was ready to go away with every waggon, to drive off with every gentleman of respectable appearance who took a cab; but no one—absolutely no one—invited me.

quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
quotes.text: My God! A whole minute of bliss! Is that not enough to fill a man's whole life?

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.text: People's memories are maybe the fuel they burn to stay alive.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.work: Colorless Tsukuru Tazaki and His Years of Pilgrimage
quotes.text: You can hide memories, but you can't erase the history that produced them.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.work: Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World
quotes.text: Once again, life had a lesson to teach me: It takes years to build up, it takes moments to destroy.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.work: Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World
quotes.text: If your confusion leads you in the right direction, the results can be uncommonly rewarding.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.work: Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World
quotes.text: Fairness is a concept that holds only in limited situations. Yet we want the concept to extend to everything, in and out of phase.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.text: Each and every moment, our bodies are on a one-way journey to collapse and deterioration, unable to turn back the clock.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.text: Loving someone is like having a mental illness that’s not covered by health insurance.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.work: South of the Border, West of the Sun
quotes.text: But I didn't understand then. That I could hurt somebody so badly she would never recover. That a person can, just by living, damage another human being beyond repair.

quotes.author: Haruki Murakami
quotes.text: Why do people have to be this lonely? What's the point of it all? Millions of people in this world, all of them yearning, looking to others to satisfy them, yet isolating themselves. Why? Was the earth put here just to nourish human loneliness?

quotes.author: Hermann Hesse
quotes.text: I wanted only to live in accord with the promptings which came from my true self. Why was that so very difficult?

quotes.author: Hermann Hesse
quotes.text: I realize today that nothing in the world is more distasteful to a man than to take the path that leads to himself.

quotes.author: Hermann Hesse
quotes.text: Each man's life represents the road toward himself, and attempt at such a road, the intimation of a path.

quotes.author: Hermann Hesse
quotes.text: Man's life seems to me like a long, weary night that would be intolerable if there were not occasionally flashes of light, the sudden brightness of which is so comforting and wonderful, that the moments of their appearance cancel out and justify the years of darkness.

quotes.author: Hermann Hesse
quotes.text: We cannot evade life's course, but we can school ourselves to be superior to fortune and also to look unflinchingly upon the most painful things.

quotes.author: Hermann Hesse
quotes.text: I am in truth the Steppenwolf that I often call myself; that beast astray who finds neither home nor joy nor nourishment in a world that is strange and incomprehensible to him.

quotes.author: Ivan Turgenev
quotes.text: Those trees, those green leaves, those high grasses screen us, hide us from all the rest of the world; no one knows where we are, what we are about—while with us is poetry, we are saturated in it, intoxicated with it, something solemn, grand, mysterious is happening to us ...

quotes.author: Ivan Turgenev
quotes.text: Egoism is suicide. The egoist withers like a solitary barren tree; but pride, ambition, as the active effort after perfection, is the source of all that is great ... Yes! a man must prune away the stubborn egoism of his personality to give it the right of self-expression.

quotes.author: Ivan Turgenev
quotes.text: After all, if you think of it, nothing is stronger in the world ... and weaker—than a word!

quotes.author: James Baldwin
quotes.work: As Much Truth As One Can Bear
quotes.text: Not everything that is faced can be changed; but nothing can be changed until it is faced.

quotes.author: James Baldwin
quotes.work: Fifth Avenue, Uptown: a Letter from Harlem
quotes.text: Anyone who has ever struggled with poverty knows how extremely expensive it is to be poor.

quotes.author: James Baldwin
quotes.text: But people can't, unhappily, invent their mooring posts, their lovers and their friends, anymore than they can invent their parents. Life gives these and also takes them away and the great difficulty is to say Yes to life.

quotes.author: James Baldwin
quotes.text: For, while the tale of how we suffer, and how we are delighted, and how we may triumph is never new, it always must be heard. There isn't any other tale to tell, it's the only light we've got in all this darkness.

quotes.author: James Baldwin
quotes.text: The primary distinction of the artist is that he must actively cultivate that state which most men, necessarily, must avoid: the state of being alone.

quotes.author: James Baldwin
quotes.work: The Precarious Vogue of Ingmar Bergman
quotes.text: All art is a kind of confession, more or less oblique. All artists, if they are to survive, are forced, at last, to tell the whole story, to vomit the anguish up.

quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.text: The hero of my tale, whom I love with all the power of my soul, whom I have tried to portray in all his beauty, who has been, is, and will be beautiful, is Truth.

quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.text: Harder and more blessed than all else is to love this life in one's sufferings, in undeserved sufferings.

quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy
quotes.text: The happiness of men consists in life. And life is in labor.

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.text: When you wake up in the morning, tell yourself: The people I deal with today will be meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, dishonest, jealous, and surly.

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.text: You will find rest from vain fancies if you perform every act in life as though it were your last.

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.text: Never esteem anything as of advantage to you that will make you break your word or lose your self-respect.

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.text: Remember that man lives only in the present, in this fleeting instant; all the rest of his life is either past and gone, or not yet revealed.

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.text: Men seek retreats for themselves, houses in the country, sea-shores, and mountains; and thou too art wont to desire such things very much. But this is altogether a mark of the most common sort of men, for it is in thy power whenever thou shalt choose to retire into thyself.

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.text: Death hangs over thee: whilst yet thou livest, whilst thou mayest, be good.

quotes.author: Natsume Sōseki
quotes.work: To the Spring Equinox and Beyond
quotes.text: He argued that when the truth is not known, we desire to know it, but once we do know it, there are not a few cases in which we repent our knowing and envy that earlier time when we lived blissfully ignorant.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: The weak fear happiness itself. They can harm themselves on cotton wool.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: Unable as I was to feel the least particle of confidence in my ability to speak and act like a human being, I kept my solitary agonies locked in my breast.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: The one thing I must avoid is becoming offensive in their eyes: I shall be nothing, the wind, the sky.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: I know that I am liked by other people, but I seem to be deficient in the faculty to love others.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: Society. I felt as though even I were beginning at last to acquire some vague notion of what it meant. It is a struggle between one individual to another, a then-and-there struggle, in which the immediate triumph is everything

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: My unhappiness stemmed entirely from my own vices, and I had no way of fighting anybody.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: I can't even guess myself what it must be to live the life of a human being.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: All I feel are the assaults of apprehension and terror at the thought that I am the only one who is entirely unlike the rest.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: The world, after all, was still a place of bottomless horror. It was by no means a place of childlike simplicity where everything could be settled by a simple then-and-there decision.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: I am afraid because I can so clearly foresee my own life rotting away of itself, like a leaf that rots without falling, while I pursue my round of existence from day to day.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: To wait. In our lives we know joy, anger, sorrow, and a hundred other emotions, but these emotions all together occupy a bare one percent of our time. The remaining ninety-nine percent is just living in waiting.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: I must go on living. And, though it may be childish of me, I can't go on in simple compliance. From now on I must struggle with the world.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: It is painful for the plant which is myself to live in the atmosphere and light of this world. Somewhere an element is lacking which would permit me to continue.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: To be alive. To be alive. An intolerably immense undertaking before which one can only gasp in apprehension.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: Last year nothing happened / The year before nothing happened / And the year before that nothing happened.

quotes.author: Osamu Dazai
quotes.text: Humanity? Don't be silly. I know. It is knocking down your fellow-men for the sake of your own happiness.

quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.text: And the point is, to live everything. Live the questions now. Perhaps you will then gradually, without noticing it, live along some distant day into the answer.

quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.text: If your daily life seems poor, do not blame it; blame yourself, tell yourself that you are not poet enough to call forth its riches; for to the creator there is no poverty and no poor indifferent place.

quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.text: If only we arrange our life according to that principle which counsels us that we must hold to the difficult, then that which now still seems to us the most alien will become what we most trust and find most faithful.

quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.text: No experience has been too unimportant, and the smallest event unfolds like a fate, and fate itself is like a wonderful, wide fabric in which every thread is guided by an infinitely tender hand and laid alongside another thread and is held and supported by a hundred others.

quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.text: Love is something difficult and it is more difficult than other things because in other conflicts nature herself enjoins men to collect themselves, to take themselves firmly in the hand with all their strength, while in the heightening of love the impulse is to give oneself wholly away.

quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.work: Selected Letters of Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.text: What is required of us is that we love the difficult and learn to deal with it. In the difficult are the friendly forces, the hands that work on us.

quotes.author: Rainer Maria Rilke
quotes.text: The work of the eyes is done. Go now and do the heart-work on the images imprisoned within you.

quotes.author: Samuel Beckett
quotes.text: If I could sleep I might make love. I'd go into the woods. My eyes would see … the sky, the earth. I'd run, run, they wouldn't catch me.

quotes.author: Samuel Beckett
quotes.text: Yes, there were times when I forgot not only who I was, but that I was, forgot to be.

quotes.author: Samuel Beckett
quotes.text: To decompose is to live too, I know, I know, don't torment me, but one sometimes forgets.

quotes.author: Samuel Beckett
quotes.text: Where now? Who now? When now? Unquestioning. I, say I. Unbelieving. Questions, hypotheses, call them that. Keep going, going on, call that going, call that on.

quotes.author: Samuel Beckett
quotes.text: But he had turned, little by little, a disturbance into words, he had made a pillow of old words, for his head.

quotes.author: Samuel Beckett
quotes.text: Then at night rest in the quiet house, there are no roads, no streets any more, you lie down by a window opening on refuge, the little sounds come that demand nothing, ordain nothing, explain nothing, propound nothing, and the short necessary night is soon ended

quotes.author: Seneca the Younger
quotes.work: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter II: On discursiveness in reading
quotes.text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.

quotes.author: Seneca the Younger
quotes.work: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter IV: On the terrors of death
quotes.text: Most men ebb and flow in wretchedness between the fear of death and the hardships of life; they are unwilling to live, and yet they do not know how to die.

quotes.author: Seneca the Younger
quotes.work: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter IV: On the terrors of death
quotes.text: No man can have a peaceful life who thinks too much about lengthening it.

quotes.author: Seneca the Younger
quotes.work: Moral Letters to Lucilius, Letter XXIV: On despising death
quotes.text: It is indeed foolish to be unhappy now because you may be unhappy at some future time.

quotes.author: Simone Weil
quotes.work: Draft for a Statement of Human Obligation
quotes.text: The reality of this world is necessity. The part of man which is in this world is the part which is in bondage to necessity and subject to the misery of need.

quotes.author: Simone Weil
quotes.text: When we are the victims of illusion we do not feel it to be an illusion but a reality. It is the same perhaps with evil. Evil when we are in its power is not felt as evil but as a necessity, or even a duty.

quotes.author: Simone Weil
quotes.text: To listen to someone is to put oneself in his place while he is speaking. To put oneself in the place of someone whose soul is corroded by affliction, or in near danger of it, is to annihilate oneself.

quotes.author: Simone Weil
quotes.text: What man needs is silence and warmth; what he is given is an icy pandemonium.

quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.text: It belongs to the imperfection of everything human that man can only attain his desire by passing through its opposite.

quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.text: It is perfectly true, as the philosophers say, that life must be understood backwards. But they forget the other proposition, that it must be lived forwards.

quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.text: Since my earliest childhood a barb of sorrow has lodged in my heart. As long as it stays I am ironic — if it is pulled out I shall die.

quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.text: It is the duty of the human understanding to understand that there are things which it cannot understand, and what those things are.

quotes.author: Virginia Woolf
quotes.text: The beauty of the world which is so soon to perish, has two edges, one of laughter, one of anguish, cutting the heart asunder.

quotes.author: Virginia Woolf
quotes.text: Life for both sexes — and I looked at them, shouldering their way along the pavement — is arduous, difficult, a perpetual struggle. It calls for gigantic courage and strength. More than anything, perhaps, creatures of illusion as we are, it calls for confidence in oneself.

quotes.author: Virginia Woolf
quotes.text: The mind receives a myriad impressions — trivial, fantastic, evanescent, or engraved with the sharpness of steel.

quotes.author: Virginia Woolf
quotes.text: Let us record the atoms as they fall upon the mind in the order in which they fall, let us trace the pattern, however disconnected and incoherent in appearance, which each sight or incident scores upon the consciousness.

quotes.author: Virginia Woolf
quotes.text: She felt this thing that she called life terrible, hostile, and quick to pounce on you if you gave it a chance.

quotes.author: Virginia Woolf
quotes.text: What is the meaning of life? That was all — a simple question; one that tended to close in on one with years. The great revelation had never come. The great revelation perhaps never did come. Instead there were little daily miracles, illuminations, matches struck unexpectedly in the dark; here was one.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.text: At no time are we ever in such complete possession of a journey, down to its last nook and cranny, as when we are busy with preparations for it.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.text: My "act" has ended by becoming an integral part of my nature, I told myself. It's no longer an act.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.work: Death in Midsummer, and Other Stories
quotes.text: By means of microscopic observation and astronomical projection the lotus flower can become the foundation for an entire theory of the universe and an agent whereby we may perceive the Truth.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.text: Perfect purity is possible if you turn your life into a line of poetry written with a splash of death.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.text: In its essence, any art that relies on words makes use of their ability to eat away — of their corrosive function — just as etching depends on the corrosive power of nitric acid.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.text: Only through the group, I realised — through sharing the suffering of the group — could the body reach that height of existence that the individual alone could never attain.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.text: The most appropriate type of daily life for me was a day-by-day world destruction; peace was the most difficult and abnormal state to live in.

quotes.author: Yukio Mishima
quotes.work: The Temple of the Golden Pavilion
quotes.text: When people concentrate on the idea of beauty, they are, without realizing it, confronted with the darkest thoughts that exist in this world
